es.title: Hacia un Lamine Yamal más maduro y racional: "Ya no me hace sufrir"
es.description: A la edad que irrumpió Lamine Yamal como un cohete propulsado, nadie, ni siquiera el propio Leo Messi había sacado todavía la cabeza. A sus 19 años, el de Rocafonda sigue siendo un adolescente, pero ya con una madurez futbolística impropia de su edad. En SPORT analizamos con el experto en alto rendimiento Xesco Espar (exentrenador del Barça de balonmano) y con el fisioterapeuta y readaptador Juanjo Brau, también con un pasado brillante en el FC Barcelona la evolución de Lamine Yamal en los últimos meses. Vídeo ID: 135786737 "Sí que noto un Lamine diferente, más pausado y tranquilo, sin aquella necesidad de salirse siempre", explica Espar sobre el canterano azulgrana. Una buena muestra de su madurez también fue cómo encajó no ganar el Balón de Oro. El año pasado, el propio Lamine admitió que le había sentado mal, pero que le fue bien para crecer. Este año, y pese a considerar que se lo merecía, tuvo una respuesta muy elegante, con felicitación al ganador, Harry Kane, y un augurio que seguro hará realidad: "Llegará mi momento". “Lamine está entrando en una dinámica muy buena. Así como el verano anterior dudábamos un poco si veíamos que se obcecaba por no marcar gol, ahora participa más en las asistencias. Evoluciona y no sufro demasiado", añade Espar sobre el de Rocafonda. Está claro que Lamine Yamal es muy ambicioso, como todos los genios futbolísticos y no ser diferencial en algún partido le va a 'enfadar' durante toda su carrera y le va a llevar a querer superarse y a ser mejor, como explicó, con una claridad impropia de su edad, en 'Universo Valdano'. Pero la cuestión está en cómo lo gestiona. Y ahí está una evolución que no ha pasado desapercibida. La comparación con Leo Messi Tampoco para Juanjo Brau, quien augura que “Lamine es un chaval que cada vez sabrá interpretar mas el juego y su situación en el juego, que se dosificará, que correrá no todas las carreras, sino la buena, que sabrá estar bien situado y leerá los partidos mejor. Y más con su enorme talento". Image ID: 135906213 Juanjo Brau y Leo Messi FCB /clip/e7138f0a-076d-4df1-b2af-e5b10b6d43df_source-aspect-ratio_default_0_x1000y375.jpg 2000 1125 En este sentido, Juanjo Brau recuerda a Leo Messi, de quien tuvo el orgullo de estar junto a él en los mejores años de su trayectoria futbolística y en un Barça irrepetible. "Tener menos desgaste físico pasa por ser más inteligente futbolísticamente. A Leo cuando lo veías andar la gente decía: 'Defendemos con 10'. Y no era verdad. Si estábamos organizados, cuando teníamos la pelota lo que pasaba es que jugábamos con 14”, sentencia Brau.

pt.title: Hospitalização Domiciliária da ULS Lezíria celebra sete anos a cuidar dos doentes em casa
pt.description: A Unidade de Hospitalização Domiciliária (UHD) da ULS Lezíria assinalou, esta quinta-feira, 29 de outubro, sete anos de atividade, com a realização da sua 5.ª Conferência, no Hospital Distrital de Santarém. A iniciativa destacou a importância de um modelo de cuidados que permite levar o hospital até à casa dos doentes. A hospitalização domiciliária é uma alternativa ao internamento hospitalar convencional, permitindo que doentes com necessidade de cuidados hospitalares possam receber acompanhamento médico e de enfermagem na sua própria habitação, desde que estejam reunidas as condições clínicas e sociais necessárias. Este modelo apresenta vantagens significativas, sobretudo para pessoas idosas ou com maior fragilidade, que podem permanecer no conforto do seu lar, próximas da família e das suas rotinas, evitando o impacto emocional e físico associado a um internamento hospitalar. Cuidar melhor e otimizar os recursos hospitalares Para além dos benefícios para os doentes e respetivas famílias, a hospitalização domiciliária desempenha um papel importante na gestão dos recursos do Serviço Nacional de Saúde. Ao permitir que determinados doentes recebam cuidados hospitalares em casa, contribui para libertar camas nos hospitais, aumentando a capacidade de resposta a situações agudas, urgentes ou de maior complexidade clínica. Importa salientar que não se trata de uma redução dos cuidados prestados, mas de uma forma diferente de os assegurar, mantendo o acompanhamento por profissionais de saúde e a possibilidade de regresso ao hospital sempre que a situação clínica o justifique. Sete anos de experiência ao serviço da comunidade A 5.ª Conferência da UHD constituiu um momento de reflexão e partilha de experiências, incluindo a apresentação de um livro dedicado à hospitalização domiciliária, o testemunho da Unidade de Hospitalização Domiciliária do Hospital de Cascais Dr. José de Almeida e um balanço dos sete anos de atividade da unidade de Santarém. Num contexto de crescente pressão sobre os serviços hospitalares e de envelhecimento da população, a hospitalização domiciliária afirma-se como uma resposta cada vez mais relevante, conciliando a humanização dos cuidados com a eficiência dos serviços de saúde. Sete anos depois, a UHD da ULS Lezíria demonstra que é possível cuidar com qualidade e segurança para além das paredes do hospital, colocando o doente no centro da prestação de cuidados. Porque o mais importante não é o lugar onde se cuida, mas a qualidade, a segurança e a dignidade com que se cuida. O conteúdo Hospitalização Domiciliária da ULS Lezíria celebra sete anos a cuidar dos doentes em casa aparece primeiro em Jornal O Almeirinense.

sg.title: Canisienne Kanazawa in Ishikawa: Winter Crab Takes Center Stage at an Intimate Eight-Seat Counter in the Nishi Chaya District
sg.description: KANAZAWA, Japan, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kanazawa Biyori, a regional media outlet rooted in the Hokuriku region of northwestern Japan, reports not only on well-known landmarks but also on the food, culture and traditions that give Hokuriku its character. From early November to the end of December, Canisienne Kanazawa (known in Japanese as Kanijennu Kanazawa), a Nishi Chaya District restaurant specializing in live crab, will serve a winter-only course. Located in one of the city's three geisha districts, the restaurant seats just eight guests at a counter, where chefs work in full view of diners. Ahead of the winter course, Kanazawa Biyori sampled the restaurant's autumn tasting course featuring both horsehair crab and red snow crab. Crab from the autumn tasting course at Canisienne Kanazawa, presented by the chef (Photo: Kanazawa Biyori) A Meal That Begins With Live Crab For many people, winter crab in Kanazawa means kōbako-gani, the female snow crab, and Kanō-gani, the regional brand name for male snow crab landed in Ishikawa Prefecture. We visited Canisienne Kanazawa after hearing that it offers a different way to enjoy crab in a city so closely tied to it. Sashimi, charcoal-grilled crab and shabu-shabu (crab swished briefly through hot broth) are among the many crab dishes served at the counter, and as crab lovers, we arrived with high expectations. Our tasting course opened with live crab brought out in a large tub, an impressive sight in itself. The best part, however, was still to come. A chef expertly prepared the crab right in front of us, breaking it down for each dish. For sashimi, the meat was dipped in cold water until it opened like a flower in bloom. Some pieces were grilled slowly over charcoal so they stayed moist, while others were cooked as shabu-shabu at just the right moment. We found ourselves absorbed in watching the chef transform the crab into one dish after another. Two Crabs, Many Flavors The sashimi paired horsehair crab with red snow crab, served with two dipping sauces so we could compare them side by side. Both had the juicy, springy texture of crab that was alive moments before, while the red snow crab in particular stood out for its sweetness. We were surprised by how different the two tasted. Grilled over charcoal, the crab developed a rich, smoky aroma and a sweetness unlike that of the sashimi. It was served with a citrus-based ponzu sauce blended with kani miso, the crab's rich tomalley. The red snow crab claws, cooked as shabu-shabu, were wonderfully plump. In the horsehair crab shabu-shabu, a gentle sweetness gave way to the aroma of matsutake mushrooms. That the flavor could change so much with each cooking method showed just how versatile crab can be. Another dish that stayed with us was abalone liver with kani miso, served bubbling hot. Bread dipped into the hot mixture soaked up its deep, savory flavor and sweetness. It was so satisfying that we could have happily kept eating it, and it became one of our favorites. The course also made room for local flavors. One was an appetizer made with black abalone from Wajima on the Noto Peninsula, whelk (baigai), chestnuts and sea urchin. A seasonal platter and hasumushi, a steamed dish of grated lotus root and nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) from Noto, were also served. Tasting Ishikawa's food beyond crab was another pleasure. Crab Through the Final Course The closing dishes were just as lavish. Kanitama, a crab and egg dish, was made so generously that nearly every spoonful was full of crab meat. Adding salmon roe or a little more kani miso let us change the flavor as we ate. Next came zosui, rice simmered in broth, also filled with crab. The matsutake broth gave off a gentle aroma, and although we were already full, we could not put down our chopsticks. To finish, we had matcha and warabi mochi, a soft, jelly-like confection made from bracken starch. The warabi mochi was made by hand at the counter, and we gladly finished every last bite. Two Hours of Sound, Scent and Flavor For about two hours, we took in the sound of the chef preparing the crab, the scent of charcoal and a steady stream of freshly made dishes. Throughout the meal, we enjoyed the differences in the crab's sweetness and texture and savored everything it had to give. The experience engaged all five senses. Winter Crab and the Dance of Kanazawa Geiko When Ishikawa's snow crab season opens in November, the restaurant will introduce its Winter Crab Feast Course, which runs through the end of December. The course features horsehair crab from Noto, kōbako-gani and live Kanō-gani. We would especially recommend the restaurant's approach to seasoned crab lovers. Our visit left us looking forward to the winter ahead more than ever. The restaurant also has a special course in which the meal is accompanied by a dance performed by Kanazawa geiko (geisha). The combination of fine food and graceful dance would make it an elegant way to welcome guests. Why Kanazawa Biyori Tells This Story When people think of Kanazawa in winter, crab is often among the first things that come to mind. ph.title: Canisienne Kanazawa in Ishikawa: Winter Crab Takes Center Stage at an Intimate Eight-Seat Counter in the Nishi Chaya District
ph.description: KANAZAWA, Japan, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kanazawa Biyori, a regional media outlet rooted in the Hokuriku region of northwestern Japan, reports not only on well-known landmarks but also on the food, culture and traditions that give Hokuriku its character. From early November to the end of December, Canisienne Kanazawa (known in Japanese as Kanijennu Kanazawa), a Nishi Chaya District restaurant specializing in live crab, will serve a winter-only course. Located in one of the city's three geisha districts, the restaurant seats just eight guests at a counter, where chefs work in full view of diners. Ahead of the winter course, Kanazawa Biyori sampled the restaurant's autumn tasting course featuring both horsehair crab and red snow crab. Crab from the autumn tasting course at Canisienne Kanazawa, presented by the chef (Photo: Kanazawa Biyori) A Meal That Begins With Live Crab For many people, winter crab in Kanazawa means kōbako-gani, the female snow crab, and Kanō-gani, the regional brand name for male snow crab landed in Ishikawa Prefecture. We visited Canisienne Kanazawa after hearing that it offers a different way to enjoy crab in a city so closely tied to it. Sashimi, charcoal-grilled crab and shabu-shabu (crab swished briefly through hot broth) are among the many crab dishes served at the counter, and as crab lovers, we arrived with high expectations. Our tasting course opened with live crab brought out in a large tub, an impressive sight in itself. The best part, however, was still to come. A chef expertly prepared the crab right in front of us, breaking it down for each dish. For sashimi, the meat was dipped in cold water until it opened like a flower in bloom. Some pieces were grilled slowly over charcoal so they stayed moist, while others were cooked as shabu-shabu at just the right moment. We found ourselves absorbed in watching the chef transform the crab into one dish after another. Two Crabs, Many Flavors The sashimi paired horsehair crab with red snow crab, served with two dipping sauces so we could compare them side by side. Both had the juicy, springy texture of crab that was alive moments before, while the red snow crab in particular stood out for its sweetness. We were surprised by how different the two tasted. Grilled over charcoal, the crab developed a rich, smoky aroma and a sweetness unlike that of the sashimi. It was served with a citrus-based ponzu sauce blended with kani miso, the crab's rich tomalley. The red snow crab claws, cooked as shabu-shabu, were wonderfully plump. In the horsehair crab shabu-shabu, a gentle sweetness gave way to the aroma of matsutake mushrooms. That the flavor could change so much with each cooking method showed just how versatile crab can be. Another dish that stayed with us was abalone liver with kani miso, served bubbling hot. Bread dipped into the hot mixture soaked up its deep, savory flavor and sweetness. It was so satisfying that we could have happily kept eating it, and it became one of our favorites. The course also made room for local flavors. One was an appetizer made with black abalone from Wajima on the Noto Peninsula, whelk (baigai), chestnuts and sea urchin. A seasonal platter and hasumushi, a steamed dish of grated lotus root and nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) from Noto, were also served. Tasting Ishikawa's food beyond crab was another pleasure. Crab Through the Final Course The closing dishes were just as lavish. Kanitama, a crab and egg dish, was made so generously that nearly every spoonful was full of crab meat. Adding salmon roe or a little more kani miso let us change the flavor as we ate. Next came zosui, rice simmered in broth, also filled with crab. The matsutake broth gave off a gentle aroma, and although we were already full, we could not put down our chopsticks. To finish, we had matcha and warabi mochi, a soft, jelly-like confection made from bracken starch. The warabi mochi was made by hand at the counter, and we gladly finished every last bite. Two Hours of Sound, Scent and Flavor For about two hours, we took in the sound of the chef preparing the crab, the scent of charcoal and a steady stream of freshly made dishes. Throughout the meal, we enjoyed the differences in the crab's sweetness and texture and savored everything it had to give. The experience engaged all five senses. The course features horsehair crab from Noto, kōbako-gani and live Kanō-gani. We would especially recommend the restaurant's approach to seasoned crab lovers. Our visit left us looking forward to the winter ahead more than ever. The restaurant also has a special course in which the meal is accompanied by a dance performed by Kanazawa geiko (geisha). The combination of fine food and graceful dance would make it an elegant way to welcome guests. ph.title: For Palestinian citizens of Israel, a historic vote born of fear and frustration
ph.description: SAKHNIN, Israel (AP) — For Palestinian citizens of Israel, it was a rare moment of political triumph. Hundreds of thousands voted in record numbers, giving two Arab-led parties their largest-ever number of seats in Israel's parliament. Many boycotted past elections, seeing little point. But after years of their communities being demonized or neglected, some of Israel's most marginalized citizens turned to the ballot box to fight back against the most right-wing government in the country's history. "We are here and we're not on the sidelines," declared Mansour Abbas, leader of the Ra'am party, as supporters cheered in a wedding hall Tuesday night, watching the exit polls. The surge makes them a major political force that could enable opposition parties to assemble a coalition to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But the question is whether Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, and other opponents will ally with them. Only once has an Arab-led party ever served in an Israeli government. During the campaign, Netanyahu had accused his main opponents of planning to form a coalition with them, which Eisenkot denied. Netanyahu and his allies are now turning up the anti-Arab rhetoric even further, making unproven claims that foreign powers bribed voters to back Arab-led parties. In a Thursday post on X, Netanyahu warned against any party forming a government with them, saying it would lead to the "Islamization of Israel." Palestinian grievances fueled the surge Nearly 840,000 people on Tuesday voted for Ra'am and the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-led parties, a 64% increase from the last elections in 2022, according to final results from the Central Election Committee. The parties won 19 seats in Israel's 120-member Knesset, surpassing the previous record of 15. Crowds packed polling places in Arab communities from the Negev Desert to the northern Galilee. In Tarabin, a Bedouin village in the Negev, Netanyahu's party had won majorities the past two elections. Turnout nearly doubled on Tuesday and Ra'am won 93% of the vote. The northern town of Sakhnin had Israel's highest voter turnout, at 87%. Mayor Mazen Ghnaim said voters saw it as an emergency measure to fight rising violent crime in Arab communities and incitement by Netanyahu's far-right allies. "I want to protect my constituents from being killed, my children from being attacked at their universities and Arab doctors getting attacked at hospitals," said Ghnaim, a Ra'am supporter, referring to recent incidents of anti-Arab violence. The parties worked hard to overcome past reluctance to vote among Palestinians, who have long felt ignored in the halls of power. They held community meetings in cities and towns that Jewish-led parties mostly ignored. A grassroots movement went door-to-door in Bedouin villages to encourage women to vote. A reaction to Israel's most far-right government ever Voters and candidates said their heightened participation did not reflect faith in Israeli democracy — it was a sign of desperation to unseat Netanyahu. Two of his far-right allies, Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, are responsible for some of Israel's most extreme policies and anti-Arab incitement. Ben Gvir, the national security minister, raised alarm on Election Day over Arab turnout, telling his supporters, "If you want this country to remain Jewish and Zionist … then get out and vote!" The rhetoric, also echoed by Netanyahu and Smotrich, may have only galvanized Arab voters. "We see the government going from bad to worse," 52-year-old Awni Zoabi said after voting in Nazareth. "We want to live, we want a future for our children, and we want a future for ourselves." The parties offer different visions Palestinians who managed to stay in Israel after the 1948 war surrounding its creation — when hundreds of thousands were expelled or fled — today, along with their descendants, make up more than 20% of the population. They have Israeli citizenship, including the right to vote, but also feel deep solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. Ra'am and the Joint List both campaigned on combating crime and securing investment for Arab communities. But they offered different visions for how to approach the wider conflict. Ra'am made the advantages of joining a coalition government central to its pitch to voters and said little that could alienate potential Jewish allies. It placed a Jewish former police official second on its candidate list. In contrast, members of the Joint List called Israel's campaign in Gaza a genocide and compared the occupation of the West Bank to apartheid South Africa. Most Jewish Israelis ardently reject both accusations. "People are clever enough to see what's happening. Of the two options, one is proposing a genocide, and the other is proposing apartheid. These are the choices: bad or worse," said Sami Abou Shehadeh, the leader of one of the slate's parties. Strong showing doesn't guarantee a role in government Mainstream Israeli parties have long resisted partnering with Arab-led parties elected to the Knesset, portraying them as threats to Israel's Jewish character or questioning their loyalty to the state. Netanyahu's opponents welcomed Ra'am into a short-lived coalition government in 2021, in return offering investment in Arab communities and legal status for unrecognized Bedouin villages facing the threat of demolition. The Islamist party's inclusion broke a longstanding taboo and gave it newfound political influence. But in public, rather than court them, Eisenkot has set conditions, including that they profess that Israel is a Jewish and democratic state and declare Hamas a terrorist organization "to be demolished." Leaders of both parties have condemned Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel but have balked at labeling the group a terrorist organization, in part because it would appear to justify Israel's devastating campaign in Gaza. Canisienne Kanazawa in Ishikawa: Winter Crab Takes Center Stage at an Intimate Eight-Seat Counter in the Nishi Chaya District
bd.description: KANAZAWA, Japan, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kanazawa Biyori, a regional media outlet rooted in the Hokuriku region of northwestern Japan, reports not only on well-known landmarks but also on the food, culture and traditions that give Hokuriku its character. From early November to the end of December, Canisienne Kanazawa (known in Japanese as Kanijennu Kanazawa), a Nishi Chaya District restaurant specializing in live crab, will serve a winter-only course. Located in one of the city's three geisha districts, the restaurant seats just eight guests at a counter, where chefs work in full view of diners. Ahead of the winter course, Kanazawa Biyori sampled the restaurant's autumn tasting course featuring both horsehair crab and red snow crab. Crab from the autumn tasting course at Canisienne Kanazawa, presented by the chef (Photo: Kanazawa Biyori) A Meal That Begins With Live Crab For many people, winter crab in Kanazawa means kōbako-gani, the female snow crab, and Kanō-gani, the regional brand name for male snow crab landed in Ishikawa Prefecture. We visited Canisienne Kanazawa after hearing that it offers a different way to enjoy crab in a city so closely tied to it. Sashimi, charcoal-grilled crab and shabu-shabu (crab swished briefly through hot broth) are among the many crab dishes served at the counter, and as crab lovers, we arrived with high expectations. Our tasting course opened with live crab brought out in a large tub, an impressive sight in itself. The best part, however, was still to come. A chef expertly prepared the crab right in front of us, breaking it down for each dish. For sashimi, the meat was dipped in cold water until it opened like a flower in bloom. Some pieces were grilled slowly over charcoal so they stayed moist, while others were cooked as shabu-shabu at just the right moment. We found ourselves absorbed in watching the chef transform the crab into one dish after another. Two Crabs, Many Flavors The sashimi paired horsehair crab with red snow crab, served with two dipping sauces so we could compare them side by side. Both had the juicy, springy texture of crab that was alive moments before, while the red snow crab in particular stood out for its sweetness. We were surprised by how different the two tasted. Grilled over charcoal, the crab developed a rich, smoky aroma and a sweetness unlike that of the sashimi. It was served with a citrus-based ponzu sauce blended with kani miso, the crab's rich tomalley. The red snow crab claws, cooked as shabu-shabu, were wonderfully plump. In the horsehair crab shabu-shabu, a gentle sweetness gave way to the aroma of matsutake mushrooms. That the flavor could change so much with each cooking method showed just how versatile crab can be. Another dish that stayed with us was abalone liver with kani miso, served bubbling hot. Bread dipped into the hot mixture soaked up its deep, savory flavor and sweetness. It was so satisfying that we could have happily kept eating it, and it became one of our favorites. The course also made room for local flavors. One was an appetizer made with black abalone from Wajima on the Noto Peninsula, whelk (baigai), chestnuts and sea urchin. A seasonal platter and hasumushi, a steamed dish of grated lotus root and nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) from Noto, were also served. Tasting Ishikawa's food beyond crab was another pleasure. Crab Through the Final Course The closing dishes were just as lavish. Kanitama, a crab and egg dish, was made so generously that nearly every spoonful was full of crab meat. Adding salmon roe or a little more kani miso let us change the flavor as we ate. Next came zosui, rice simmered in broth, also filled with crab. The matsutake broth gave off a gentle aroma, and although we were already full, we could not put down our chopsticks. To finish, we had matcha and warabi mochi, a soft, jelly-like confection made from bracken starch. The warabi mochi was made by hand at the counter, and we gladly finished every last bite. Two Hours of Sound, Scent and Flavor For about two hours, we took in the sound of the chef preparing the crab, the scent of charcoal and a steady stream of freshly made dishes. Throughout the meal, we enjoyed the differences in the crab's sweetness and texture and savored everything it had to give. The experience engaged all five senses. Winter Crab and the Dance of Kanazawa Geiko When Ishikawa's snow crab season opens in November, the restaurant will introduce its Winter Crab Feast Course, which runs through the end of December. The course features horsehair crab from Noto, kōbako-gani and live Kanō-gani. We would especially recommend the restaurant's approach to seasoned crab lovers. Our visit left us looking forward to the winter ahead more than ever. The restaurant also has a special course in which the meal is accompanied by a dance performed by Kanazawa geiko (geisha). The combination of fine food and graceful dance would make it an elegant way to welcome guests. Why Kanazawa Biyori Tells This Story When people think of Kanazawa in winter, crab is often among the first things that come to mind. Canisienne Kanazawa presents it in a new light, with live crab turned into several different dishes right at the counter, along with ingredients from Wajima and the Noto Peninsula. Kanazawa Biyori is highlighting this restaurant because it shows that even a long-familiar local delicacy can still be discovered anew. For readers planning a winter trip to the city, we hope the restaurant will offer a chance to experience the region's crab up close. bd.title: Xinhua Silk Road: Botanee showcases Chinese solutions for global mountain bioeconomy at COP17
bd.description: BEIJING, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Botanee Group, a Chinese cosmetics enterprise, shared its sustainable development model of "research-conservation-industrialization" originating from Yunnan, China, on October 26 in Yerevan, Armenia where the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) takes place. Botanee, as a co-organiser of the mountain bioeconomy-themed side event of the COP17, also launched the Yerevan Declaration on Inclusive Mountain Bioeconomy with other partners. Centred on "conserving biodiversity, supporting sustainable community development, ensuring fair and equitable benefit-sharing, and creating opportunities for future generations," the declaration emphasizes the integration of traditional knowledge, scientific research and responsible innovation, and advocates advancing ecological conservation and livelihood improvement while respecting the rights of indigenous peoples and local communities. In her keynote address, Zhong Wei, director of public communications at Botanee Group, systematically outlined the underlying logic of the enterprise's sustainability approach. She said that as an enterprise rooted in biodiversity, Botanee recognizes that safeguarding nature means protecting the foundation of its business. To this end, Botanee has built a three-in-one sustainable beauty ecosystem centred on "research-conservation-industrialization." On the research front, Botanee has carried out 12 years of joint industry-university-research collaboration. It has screened more than 2,000 plant resources and identified 266 skincare-active species, translating the traditional uses of native Yunnan plants into standardized, traceable industrial strengths. On the conservation front, it has established a research and cultivation base at Haba Snow Mountain in Shangri-La, and carried out artificial propagation and wild reintroduction for over 20 rare plateau species, to support biodiversity. In terms of the industrialization, Botanee adopts an "enterprise + base + farming household" model, enabling farmers and herders in northwest Yunnan to earn stable incomes locally. In 2024, the characteristic plant industrial chain generated over 10 billion yuan in additional output value, with local suppliers accounting for 53.8 percent of raw material sources. This model has been included as a case in the Global Mountain Bioeconomy Framework, an action guide for global sustainable mountain development. It will continue to advance the implementation of the mountain bioeconomy declaration across global mountain regions, refine its "research-conservation-industrialization" model, and contribute to global biodiversity governance, according to Botanee. ae.title: Canisienne Kanazawa in Ishikawa: Winter Crab Takes Center Stage at an Intimate Eight-Seat Counter in the Nishi Chaya District
ae.description: KANAZAWA, Japan, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kanazawa Biyori, a regional media outlet rooted in the Hokuriku region of northwestern Japan, reports not only on well-known landmarks but also on the food, culture and traditions that give Hokuriku its character. From early November to the end of December, Canisienne Kanazawa (known in Japanese as Kanijennu Kanazawa), a Nishi Chaya District restaurant specializing in live crab, will serve a winter-only course. Located in one of the city's three geisha districts, the restaurant seats just eight guests at a counter, where chefs work in full view of diners. Ahead of the winter course, Kanazawa Biyori sampled the restaurant's autumn tasting course featuring both horsehair crab and red snow crab. Crab from the autumn tasting course at Canisienne Kanazawa, presented by the chef (Photo: Kanazawa Biyori) A Meal That Begins With Live Crab For many people, winter crab in Kanazawa means kōbako-gani, the female snow crab, and Kanō-gani, the regional brand name for male snow crab landed in Ishikawa Prefecture. We visited Canisienne Kanazawa after hearing that it offers a different way to enjoy crab in a city so closely tied to it. Sashimi, charcoal-grilled crab and shabu-shabu (crab swished briefly through hot broth) are among the many crab dishes served at the counter, and as crab lovers, we arrived with high expectations. Our tasting course opened with live crab brought out in a large tub, an impressive sight in itself. The best part, however, was still to come. A chef expertly prepared the crab right in front of us, breaking it down for each dish. For sashimi, the meat was dipped in cold water until it opened like a flower in bloom. Some pieces were grilled slowly over charcoal so they stayed moist, while others were cooked as shabu-shabu at just the right moment. We found ourselves absorbed in watching the chef transform the crab into one dish after another. Two Crabs, Many Flavors The sashimi paired horsehair crab with red snow crab, served with two dipping sauces so we could compare them side by side. Both had the juicy, springy texture of crab that was alive moments before, while the red snow crab in particular stood out for its sweetness. We were surprised by how different the two tasted. Grilled over charcoal, the crab developed a rich, smoky aroma and a sweetness unlike that of the sashimi. It was served with a citrus-based ponzu sauce blended with kani miso, the crab's rich tomalley. The red snow crab claws, cooked as shabu-shabu, were wonderfully plump. In the horsehair crab shabu-shabu, a gentle sweetness gave way to the aroma of matsutake mushrooms. That the flavor could change so much with each cooking method showed just how versatile crab can be. Another dish that stayed with us was abalone liver with kani miso, served bubbling hot. Bread dipped into the hot mixture soaked up its deep, savory flavor and sweetness. It was so satisfying that we could have happily kept eating it, and it became one of our favorites. The course also made room for local flavors. One was an appetizer made with black abalone from Wajima on the Noto Peninsula, whelk (baigai), chestnuts and sea urchin. A seasonal platter and hasumushi, a steamed dish of grated lotus root and nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) from Noto, were also served. Tasting Ishikawa's food beyond crab was another pleasure. Crab Through the Final Course The closing dishes were just as lavish. Kanitama, a crab and egg dish, was made so generously that nearly every spoonful was full of crab meat. Adding salmon roe or a little more kani miso let us change the flavor as we ate. Next came zosui, rice simmered in broth, also filled with crab. The matsutake broth gave off a gentle aroma, and although we were already full, we could not put down our chopsticks. To finish, we had matcha and warabi mochi, a soft, jelly-like confection made from bracken starch. The warabi mochi was made by hand at the counter, and we gladly finished every last bite. Two Hours of Sound, Scent and Flavor For about two hours, we took in the sound of the chef preparing the crab, the scent of charcoal and a steady stream of freshly made dishes. Throughout the meal, we enjoyed the differences in the crab's sweetness and texture and savored everything it had to give. The experience engaged all five senses. Winter Crab and the Dance of Kanazawa Geiko When Ishikawa's snow crab season opens in November, the restaurant will introduce its Winter Crab Feast Course, which runs through the end of December. The course features horsehair crab from Noto, kōbako-gani and live Kanō-gani. We would especially recommend the restaurant's approach to seasoned crab lovers. Our visit left us looking forward to the winter ahead more than ever. The restaurant also has a special course in which the meal is accompanied by a dance performed by Kanazawa geiko (geisha). The combination of fine food and graceful dance would make it an elegant way to welcome guests. Why Kanazawa Biyori Tells This Story When people think of Kanazawa in winter, crab is often among the first things that come to mind. Canisienne Kanazawa presents it in a new light, with live crab turned into several different dishes right at the counter, along with ingredients from Wajima and the Noto Peninsula. Kanazawa Biyori is highlighting this restaurant because it shows that even a long-familiar local delicacy can still be discovered anew. For readers planning a winter trip to the city, we hope the restaurant will offer a chance to experience the region's crab up close. Information Canisienne Kanazawa (Japanese name: Kanijennu Kanazawa) Courses: Winter Crab Feast Course (horsehair crab from Noto, kōbako-gani and live Kanō-gani): ¥49,000 (approximately US$310, tax included); available from early November to the end of December Winter Crab Feast with a Kanazawa Geiko Performance (English rendering by Kanazawa Biyori): Minimum charge of ¥600,000 (approximately US$3,800, tax included) for a private dinner for 6–8 guests (A separate 10% service charge applies.) (Course contents may vary depending on the fishing season and availability.) iq.title: رونالدو على مقربة من تحقيق حلم طال انتظاره
iq.description: شفق نيوز- متابعة تمكن النجم البرتغالي وقائد فريق النصر السعودي كريستيانو رونالدو من رفع رصيد أهدافه إلى 985 هدفا خلال مسيرته الكروية مع كل الأندية التي لعب لها فضلا عن المنتخب البرتغالي، وأصبح على بعد 15 هدفا فقط من الوصول إلى الهدف رقم 1000. ووصل صاروخ ماديرا إلى هدفه الـ985 بعد تسجيله ثلاثية (هاتريك) بفوز فريق النصر على ضيفه فريق الخلود، يوم أمس الخميس ضمن دوري روشن السعودي، ليقترب أكثر من الهدف 1000. وتألق قائد النصر في هذه المباراة، وأحرز ثلاثيته خلال 15 دقيقة، حيث أحرز هدف الأول والثالث للنصر، في الدقيقة 66 قبل أن يضيف هدفين آخرين في الدقيقتين 72 و81. وكان فريق الخلود قد افتتح التسجيل عن طريق لاعبه جوليان دومينغيش في الدقيقة 16، ثم عادل أنجيلو غابرييل النتيجة للنصر في الدقيقة 24. وتقدم النصر عن طريق السنغالي ساديو ماني في الدقيقة 38، قبل أن يدرك أنطوان إيسومبا التعادل للخلود في الدقيقة الثانية من الوقت بدل الضائع للشوط الأول، لينتهي النصف الأول بالتعادل 2-2. وفي الشوط الثاني، أحرز رونالدو ثلاثيته، قبل أن يعود دومينغيش ويسجل هدفه الشخصي الثاني والثالث للخلود في الدقيقة الرابعة من الوقت المحتسب بدلا من الضائع. ويطمح كريستيانو إلى تسجيل رقمه القياسي الجديد بالهدف رقم ألف في مسيرته الكروية محققا إنجازا تاريخيا سيكون من الصعب كسره في المستقبل.

iq.title: 36 لاعباً يتنافسون على لقب بطولة العراق المفتوحة للغولف في أربيل (صور)
iq.description: شفق نيوز- أربيل تحتضن مدينة أربيل منافسات النسخة الـ51 التاريخية من بطولة العراق المفتوحة للغولف، بمشاركة 36 لاعباً موزعين على ثلاث فئات، في بطولة ينظمها الاتحاد العراقي للغولف بالتعاون مع ملعب أربيل هيلز، وتستمر منافساتها ثلاثة أيام، من 29 إلى 31 من الشهر الجاري، بعد يومين من التدريبات. وقال مدير اللجنة التنظيمية للبطولة وعضو الاتحاد العراقي للغولف، محمد رياض عبد العباس، لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن البطولة الحالية تمثل النسخة الثانية بعد إعادة إحياء نشاط الاتحاد عام 2022، والنسخة الـ51 وفق التسلسل التاريخي للبطولة، موضحاً أن المشاركة تتوزع على ثلاث فئات، بينها فئة الأطفال التي تضم أربعة لاعبين، إلى جانب فئات الكبار. وأضاف أن تاريخ لعبة الغولف في العراق يعود إلى عام 1921، مع دخول البريطانيين وانتشار الشركات النفطية، إذ كانت ملاعب الغولف تُنشأ بالقرب من الحقول النفطية، وأوضح عبد العباس أن البطولة عادت بعد عام 2003، فيما استؤنفت إقامتها فعلياً عام 2025، بعد إعادة تأسيس الاتحاد، لافتاً إلى أن النسخة الحالية شهدت إقامة حفل افتتاح في 28 من الشهر الجاري، بحضور رئيس اللجنة الأولمبية الوطنية العراقية عقيل مفتن، ونائب رئيس اللجنة الأولمبية، ورئيس الاتحاد العراقي للغولف، وعدد من الشخصيات الرياضية. وأشار إلى أن البطولة تقام في ملعب أربيل هيلز، المصمم وفق معايير عالمية من قبل شركة "داي ديزاينز" البريطانية، ويضم 18 حفرة، إلا أن المنافسات تستخدم حالياً تسع حفر مرتين، لحين استكمال الملعب بنسبة 100%، مبيناً أن الملعب صُمم ليكون مؤهلاً لاستضافة بطولات رابطة محترفي الغولف (PGA)، ما يجعله من الملاعب الحديثة والمميزة على مستوى الشرق الأوسط. وتابع عبد العباس قائلاً إن البطولة تنظم وفق معايير الاتحاد الدولي للغولف ومنظمة "R&A" المعنية بقوانين اللعبة وأنظمتها، فيما يتولى إدارتها الفنية ماهر بوشماوي، الرئيس السابق للاتحاد التونسي للغولف، والحاصل على شهادة حكم من المستوى الثالث، فضلاً عن كونه منظماً معتمداً لدى الاتحادات الدولي والأفريقي والعربي. وبحسب مدير اللجنة التنظيمية للبطولة فإن المنافسات ستشهد توزيع كؤوس وميداليات على أصحاب المراكز الأولى والثانية والثالثة في الفئات الثلاث، مشيراً إلى أن المشاركة الحالية تضم لاعبين يحملون جنسيات مزدوجة، بينها العراقية والأميركية والبريطانية والأسترالية، مع تطلع الاتحاد إلى توسيع المشاركة الدولية في النسخ المقبلة. وفي ما يتعلق بواقع ملاعب الغولف في العراق، أوضح عبد العباس أن ملعب أربيل هيلز يعد أول ملعب غولف متكامل في البلاد بعد عام 2003، فيما يوجد ملعب آخر في دهوك بنظام "بار 3" ويضم تسع حفر، ويمكن استخدامه في البطولات المحلية، لكنه لا يستوفي متطلبات استضافة المنافسات الدولية. يذكر أن مدينة أربيل عاصمة إقليم كوردستان شهدت، يوم الثلاثاء الماضي، انطلاق منافسات النسخة الـ51 من بطولة العراق المفتوحة للغولف، التي تُقام على ملاعب "أربيل هيلز" للغولف، وتستمر لغاية الأول من تشرين الثاني/ نوفمبر المقبل.

eg.title: ميسي يوافق على المشاركة في مباراة اعتزال كارلوس تيفيز
eg.description: كشف الأرجنتيني كارلوس تيفيز، نجم مانشستر سيتي ومانشستر يونايتد ويوفنتوس السابق، عن حضور مواطنه ليونيل ميسي لاعب نادي إنتر ميامي مباراة اعتزاله المقرر إقامتها يوم 20 ديسمبر المقبل على ملعب لا بومبونيرا، معقل بوكا جونيورز، في حدث مرتقب يشهد مشاركة مجموعة كبيرة من نجوم كرة القدم السابقين والحاليين. وكان تيفيز قد أعلن في سبتمبر الماضي تنظيم مباراة وداعية، رغم اعتزاله كرة القدم الاحترافية عام 2021، إذ يستعد للعودة إلى المستطيل الأخضر مرة أخيرة من أجل توديع جماهير بوكا جونيورز. وأكد تيفيز، خلال ظهوره في بودكاست المدافع الإنجليزي السابق ريو فرديناند، أن ميسي سيشارك في المباراة، إلى جانب خوان رومان ريكيلمي، رئيس بوكا جونيورز الحالي، والذي سيظهر أيضًا كلاعب. وأوضح نجم الأرجنتين السابق أن المباراة ستجمع فريق بوكا جونيورز مع فريق يضم مجموعة من أقرب أصدقائه، وسط قائمة مرشحة للحضور تضم أسماء بارزة، بينها جابرييل باتيستوتا، وجيانلويجي بوفون، وإدوين فان دير سار، وسيرخيو أجويرو، وأرتورو فيدال، وباتريس إيفرا، ومارتن باليرمو، وبابلو زاباليتا، وإستيبان كامبياسو ونيكولاس بورديسو. كما يرغب تيفيز في الاستعانة بروبرتو مانشيني وكارلوس بيانكي لقيادة الفريقين من على مقاعد البدلاء، لكن هذا الأمر لم يُحسم رسميًا حتى الآن. في المقابل، لا يزال موقف البرتغالي كريستيانو رونالدو غير واضح، بعدما كشف تيفيز أن قائد منتخب البرتغال لم يرد حتى الآن على دعوته للمشاركة، رغم رغبته في جمعه مع ميسي داخل الملعب. ولا يقتصر الأمر على رونالدو، إذ تضم قائمة الأسماء التي لم تحسم موقفها أندريا بيرلو وأنخيل دي ماريا وجونزالو هيغواين ودانييلي دي روسي وجورجيو كيليني وبول بوغبا وبول سكولز وواين روني. ومن المنتظر أيضًا أن يشهد الحدث ظهور سائق فورمولا 1 فرانكو كولابينتو ونجم التنس السابق خوان مارتن ديل بوترو، إلى جانب فقرات موسيقية. ويحظى تيفيز بمكانة خاصة لدى جماهير بوكا جونيورز، بعدما سجل 94 هدفًا خلال 279 مباراة بقميص النادي، وتوج معه بـ11 لقبًا، ليحصل على فرصة الوداع أمام الجماهير التي ارتبطت به طوال مسيرته. قد يهمك أيضــــــــــــــا ميسي يتفوق على رونالدو في تصنيف أفضل 30 لاعبًا بتاريخ الكرة الذهبية.. ومبابي بالمركز 22 ميسي يتسلم تكريمًا رسميًا من ولية عهد إسبانيا خلال مراسم جوائز أميرة أستورياس

الأسواق الأوروبية والمتوسطية، مشيرا إلى جملة الأولويات التي تفرض نفسها في هذه المقاربة وهي كالتالي: -إعداد خارطة طريق تحدد الشراكات المؤسساتية والمهمات -تحديد المشاريع النموذجية القابلة للتنفيذ في المجالات ذات الأهمية القصوى -تكثيف لقاءات الأعمال ومهمات الشركات والمشاركات في المعارض المختصة -وضع آلية للمتابعة تمكن من تقييم النتائج المحققة وتعمل على معالجة التحديات التي من الممكن أن تكون عائقا مما يساهم في خلق مواطن الشغل وفرص جديدة لكلا البلدين. من جانبه، أكد الكاتب العام لوزارة الصناعة والتجارة بالسينغال على ضرورة العمل على تطوير التبادل الاقتصادي ودفع علاقات التعاون والشراكة بين الجانبين إضافة إلى خلق فرص جديدة للاستثمار مما يساهم في الارتقاء بالعلاقات الثنائية، مشيرا إلى دور الهياكل المهنية وغرف التجارة والقطاع الخاص في تحقيق جملة الأهداف المرسومة في هذا الاتجاه.
